summary: The design can reuse much of the existing machinery, but the host reconcilers are not toolkit-only and their ownership models differ. The highest risks are unintended wikitoolkit changes, non-atomic YAML mutations, inaccurate availability/API reporting, and incomplete migration of existing consumers.

suggestions.title: Add toolkit-only host reconciliation
suggestions.rationale: Claude `_install_mcp_json`, Codex `_install_mcp`, and Google `_install_mcp` all also install or refresh wikitoolkit; Google additionally writes the Antigravity plugin configuration. Calling them from `parrot toolkits` would mutate artifacts explicitly outside this command’s ownership. Add per-host toolkit-only reconcilers or an explicit mode that preserves wikitoolkit.

suggestions.title: Model host asymmetry explicitly
suggestions.rationale: The proposal assumes every host exposes `_is_managed_toolkit_entry`, but Codex has no equivalent: it detects foreign entries through TOML table names and a managed marker block, while Google has both a user-level config and a repository plugin. Define a host adapter contract for inspect, reconcile, collision warnings, and paths instead of importing private helpers as if they were symmetric.

suggestions.title: Handle Claude approvals selectively
suggestions.rationale: `_managed_server_names` always includes wikitoolkit, and `_install_mcp_approval` authorizes every managed name. `_uninstall_mcp_approval` is designed around the full integration uninstall. Disable/uninstall must snapshot only confirmed-managed toolkit entries before YAML mutation and remove only their approvals; otherwise the new command may authorize wikitoolkit or remove approval for a foreign colliding server.

suggestions.title: Preflight mutations before seeding
suggestions.rationale: `seed_toolkit_sections` catches `ValueError` while loading an existing config, appends to the malformed file, and only then raises on reload. It also seeds valid names when the request contains an unknown name, contradicting the required all-or-nothing unknown-name behavior. Validate the complete name set and existing YAML before writing, then use an atomic replacement for the local edit.

suggestions.title: Choose a real comment-preserving YAML strategy
suggestions.rationale: The current implementation uses PyYAML `safe_load`; the package has no round-trip YAML dependency, and `seed_toolkit_sections` only appends text. Toggle and removal cannot safely use `safe_dump` if operator comments and formatting must survive. Either add and approve a round-trip parser or define a narrowly constrained lexical editor with tests for nested comments, quoted keys, and section removal.

suggestions.title: Make dependency availability metadata explicit
suggestions.rationale: `available_templates()` exposes only YAML file stems and current template metadata contains summary/LLM flags, not required distributions. Querysource’s optional dependency is loaded through `_qs`, while `QuerysourceToolkit.__init__` catches its ImportError and defers failure until `_open`; the server’s current import hint only covers scraping/browsing. Add non-importing requirement/install-hint metadata and distinguish “template installed” from “runtime dependency available.”

suggestions.title: Derive database-toolkit information from the actual contract
suggestions.rationale: The accepted tool-name list is not aligned with the current implementation/tests: the class methods include `validate_query`, `get_table_metadata`, and `test_connection`, while existing tests assert a four-tool default set including `dq_validate_database_query`; `save_result` is conditional on `output_dir`. Verify generated names against `get_tools()` and avoid publishing a stale hard-coded list in the template or CLI.

suggestions.title: Define Google’s target and state precisely
suggestions.rationale: Google’s default MCP file is `~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json`, while the installer also maintains `.agents/plugins/parrot/mcp_config.json`. A repository-scoped `--host google` command therefore needs an explicit `--mcp-config` or a documented rule for inspecting and updating both files; otherwise `list` and CI results will depend on the operator’s home directory and plugin state.

suggestions.title: Audit all builtin consumers in the same change
suggestions.rationale: Removing `BUILTIN_TOOLKITS` affects more than the three installers. `examples/dev_loop/mcp_wiring.py` documents and tests merged builtins, `local_cli.py` still advertises builtins, and the main toolkit documentation says the three names work without YAML. Update these consumers and examples together, with a repository-wide search for builtin assumptions as an acceptance check.

suggestions.title: Add a cross-host command matrix before removing old flags
suggestions.rationale: Current tests strongly cover Claude’s old seeding flags and database-toolkit behavior, while Codex/Google tests opened here focus on conventions rather than toolkit reconciliation. Add CLI and filesystem tests for list-without-class-import, no-TTY failures, unknown-name atomicity, malformed YAML preservation, enable/disable/uninstall, foreign collisions, Google dual-config behavior, Claude approval cleanup, and secret-free output.
